claim: The model-coherence composition. An authored MODEL feeds two paths: consumers CONSUME it live rather than copying its facts, and where the model owns the fact it can EMIT downstream artifacts. Consumption flows into a CORRESPONDENCE check — model against world — which DERIVEs its verdict from stable identities where an independent join exists; on disagreement a GATE enforces the modeled property. Solid path: the required composition. Dashed attachment: a useful enhancement, not required for the capability.
topology: Required model-consume-correspondence-decision path; optional emit and derive attachments remain dashed; gate on disagreement.
required_terms: Solid: required composition. Dashed: useful enhancement, not required for the capability.
bw_encoding: Black strokes and text; pale gray headers only. Dashed paths retain optional, missing, or forbidden semantics where explicitly labeled. Position, containment, line weight, and written labels carry distinctions without color.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames.
alt:
A model of an authored fact sits at the top. The load-bearing solid path runs MODEL to
    CONSUME (read the model live rather than copy its facts) to CORRESPONDENCE (compare model against the
    world) to a disagreement decision that gates the disagreement or passes it as valid. Two enhancements
    attach as dashed, open-arrowed strengtheners: EMIT (generate downstream artifacts from the model) and
    DERIVE (compute correspondence from stable identities). They are useful but not required: a descriptive
    model may stay advisory.
